Bharti Airtel shares jump after Q2 show; CLSA hikes target, HSBC maintains Buy; check fresh targets
sum: Shares of Bharti Airtel Ltd rose over 2 per cent on Friday, November 6, after the telecom major reported a 31 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit for the September quarter (Q2FY27).

The stock was trading at Rs 2,101.40 on the NSE, up Rs 44.50 or 2.16 per cent. It opened at Rs 2,120 and touched an intraday high of Rs 2,120 and a low of Rs 2,076.20. The company's market capitalisation stood at around Rs 12.58 lakh crore.
Bharti Airtel announced its Q2 results after market hours on Thursday.
The company's consolidated net profit rose to Rs 8,887.5 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 6,791.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Revenue from operations increased 16.7 per cent YoY to Rs 60,878 crore from Rs 52,145 crore in Q2FY26.

Operating performance also remained strong. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) grew 17.8 per cent YoY to Rs 35,240 crore from Rs 29,919 crore in the year-ago quarter.

India revenue increased 9.4 per cent YoY to Rs 42,308 crore. The mobile business continued to benefit from premiumisation, higher average revenue per user (ARPU) and additions in smartphone data customers.

HSBC stock: Q3 profit jumps as buyback and outlook hold
sum: HSBC Holdings reported stronger third-quarter results on October 27, 2026, while keeping its financial targets unchanged. In its 3Q26 earnings release, the bank said profit before tax increased 32 percent from a year earlier to 9.6 billion US dollars.

The headline increase included a favorable 1.4 billion US dollar effect from notable items, mainly because legal provisions recorded in the third quarter of 2025 did not recur. Excluding notable items, constant-currency profit before tax rose by 0.9 billion US dollars to 10.0 billion US dollars. Profit after tax increased 38 percent to 7.6 billion US dollars.

Revenue rose 0.8 billion US dollars to 18.6 billion US dollars, driven mainly by banking net interest income. HSBC also cited higher fee and other income in Corporate and Institutional Banking, Wealth and other businesses. Revenue excluding notable items on a constant-currency basis increased to 18.7 billion US dollars.

Net interest income advanced 6 percent to 9.3 billion US dollars, while banking net interest income increased by 0.6 billion US dollars to 11.7 billion US dollars. The net interest margin held steady at 1.57 percent. Expected credit losses fell 17 percent to 0.8 billion US dollars, although the bank continued to monitor commercial real estate and other credit exposures.

HSBC stock traded at 15.75 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:47 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 4.30 percent above the Xetra close of Tuesday, November 3, at 15.10 euros. Investors can follow the real-time quote of HSBC stock.

The board approved a third interim dividend of 0.10 US dollars per share. HSBC completed a 1 billion US dollar buyback on September 28 and intends to start another repurchase of up to 1 billion US dollars, which it expects to complete by the announcement of its 2026 full-year results.

Management retained its target for banking net interest income of at least 46 billion US dollars in 2026. It also maintained a return on average tangible equity target of 17 percent or better for 2026 through 2028, excluding notable items, and a 50 percent dividend payout ratio target through 2028.

Beiersdorf stock faces HSBC downgrade as NIVEA concerns persist
sum: Beiersdorf stock faced a more cautious analyst view after HSBC downgraded the company to Hold from Buy on Monday, November 2, and cut its price target to 88 euros from 90 euros. Investing.com, citing Reuters, said the bank saw slower NIVEA shopper sales and less room for margin improvement in 2027.

HSBC's revised view followed Beiersdorf's third-quarter update from October 27. Group organic sales declined 1.3 percent, while NIVEA sales fell 4.9 percent organically. The bank said the quarter missed its estimate for the group, although the consumer division performed better than expected.

The pressure was concentrated in the core NIVEA business and the tesa electronics unit. A commercial dispute in Russia contributed 170 basis points to NIVEA's decline, according to the report, while management said the dispute had been resolved and normal business should resume in the fourth quarter. Retailer disputes, destocking and a difficult comparison with last year's launches are still expected to weigh on NIVEA.

HSBC cut its 2027 earnings-per-share forecast to 4.17 euros from 4.22 euros and lowered its adjusted operating-margin estimate to 12 percent from 12.2 percent. The bank said Beiersdorf's restrained pricing strategy could make it harder to offset higher raw-material and packaging costs, increasing the uncertainty around future margin expansion.

Beiersdorf's portfolio also showed areas of resilience. Derma sales rose 10.6 percent organically in the third quarter, supported by Eucerin and Aquaphor, while La Prairie advanced 8.5 percent. Healthcare sales increased 5.7 percent. These businesses provide a counterweight to NIVEA's weakness, but HSBC does not expect a clear acceleration in NIVEA shopper sales or a substantial margin recovery over the next 12 months.

Management has kept its 2026 outlook unchanged. The company continues to expect a low-single-digit organic sales decline at group level and an EBIT margin excluding special factors of at least 11.8 percent. The Consumer segment is expected to post an EBIT margin of at least 11.0 percent. For investors, the key test is whether the turnaround can bring sell-in closer to sell-out while restoring healthier inventory levels by year-end.

HSBC stock holds targets as third-quarter profit rises 32 percent
sum: HSBC Holdings kept its financial targets unchanged after reporting a stronger third quarter, while a new dividend and planned buyback reinforced its capital-return strategy. In its HSBC 3Q 2026 earnings release dated Tuesday, October 27, the bank said third-quarter profit before tax rose 32 percent year over year to 9.6 billion US dollars.

HSBC stock traded at 15.34 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:01 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 0.32 percent below the Xetra close of Monday, November 2, at 15.39 euros. The comparison uses the completed Xetra session rather than the prior-session close.

The board approved a third interim dividend of 0.10 US dollars per share. HSBC also said it intends to begin a share buyback of up to 1 billion US dollars, following completion of the previous 1 billion US dollar programme on September 28.

The latest release adds a reported-profit perspective to the bank's adjusted performance. Profit before tax excluding notable items reached 10.0 billion US dollars, while annualised return on average tangible equity was 18.2 percent on the same basis. Reported profit benefited in part from the non-recurrence of 1.4 billion US dollars in legal provisions recorded in the year-earlier quarter.

HSBC continues to target banking net interest income of at least 46 billion US dollars in 2026 and a return on tangible equity of at least 17 percent for 2026 through 2028, excluding notable items. The bank also retained its 50 percent target dividend payout ratio and expects target-basis operating expenses to grow by about 1 percent in 2026.

HSBC stock heads into Dubai finance forum after strong quarter
sum: HSBC stock enters the week of Monday, November 2, with HSBC Asset Management CEO Nicolas Moreau listed among the speakers at Dubai Future Finance Week. The event runs from November 2 to 6 and will bring together financial institutions, investors and policymakers, according to Fast Company Middle East.

The program includes more than 85 events, 12 flagship forums and more than 850 expected speakers. The Dubai FinTech Summit on November 2 and 3 is the week's main event, while later sessions focus on sustainable finance, Islamic finance, private capital and tokenized markets.

HSBC's latest operating update provides the financial context for the conference appearance. The bank reported third-quarter revenue of 18.7 billion US dollars and profit before tax of 10.0 billion US dollars excluding notable items for the period ended September 30, 2026. Annualised return on tangible equity reached 18.8 percent year to date, also excluding notable items, according to HSBC Investors.

Management reiterated its medium-term targets, including revenue growth of 5 percent by 2028, return on tangible equity of 17 percent or better and dividends equal to 50 percent of earnings per share, subject to the stated exclusions. The bank also approved a third interim dividend of 10 US cents per share for 2026.

HSBC stock traded at 15.22 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:00:33 CET on Sunday, November 1, 0.78 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, October 30, at 15.34 euros. The real-time quote of HSBC stock reflects the Sunday trading snapshot.

HSBC shares slide almost 7% as revenue misses and wealth stalls despite 32% profit jump
sum: - HSBC reported third-quarter results on Tuesday, October 27, and the shares fell almost 7% even though profit rose sharply.

- HSBC shares fell almost 7% after Q3 revenue of around $18.6bn missed forecasts and wealth revenue stalled, overshadowing a 32% jump in pre-tax profit to around $9.6bn and a fresh buyback of up to $1bn. Guidance was only reaffirmed, not upgraded.

The sell-off shows how much was already priced into HSBC after a strong run. Without a guidance upgrade, a revenue miss and stalled wealth growth were enough to trigger profit-taking. The read-across for Hong Kong and Asian banks is margin pressure: costlier time deposits threaten interest income just as the Fed’s hiking path keeps funding costs high. Oil matters indirectly, since inflation and rate uncertainty linked to the Iran war is weighing on bank valuations broadly, and HSBC is already setting aside provisions for the Middle East conflict. The Basel 3.1 capital boost from January 2027 gives HSBC room to expand buybacks, which could limit further downside once the disappointment fades.
HSBC delivered a big profit jump and another $1 billion buyback, but a revenue miss, flat wealth income and no upgrade to its targets were enough to send the shares sharply lower.
- HSBC shares fell almost 7% on Tuesday after third-quarter revenue of around $18.6 billion missed forecasts of roughly $19.1 billion, and adjusted EPS of $2.10 missed $2.22.
- Pre-tax profit rose 32% to around $9.6 billion, helped by the absence of last year’s legal provisions. Excluding notable items, it rose about 10% to around $10 billion.
- Wealth revenue was flat at around $2.7 billion after strong growth in the first half. Net interest income rose 6% but was slightly below expectations.

Top Utilities Stocks to Watch: HSBC’s Preferred Picks
sum: Investing.com -- HSBC has identified five preferred utilities stocks positioned to benefit from surging electricity demand driven by data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure. The investment bank rates all five companies as Buy, citing above-average growth prospects and strong execution capabilities in an evolving power landscape.

The utilities sector is experiencing a transformation as electricity demand accelerates, particularly in regions attracting large data center developments. HSBC's preferred stocks demonstrate rate base growth rates well above historical averages, with several companies projecting demand increases of 40% to 80% by 2030. The bank's selections span integrated electric utilities, transmission-focused operators, and diversified energy infrastructure companies across multiple U.S. markets.

1. Entergy (ETR) - HSBC rates Entergy as Buy with a target price of USD123.50, implying 17.5% upside. The integrated electric utility operates in Louisiana, Arkansas, Texas, Mississippi and New Orleans. HSBC forecasts 2026-30 rate base growth of 16% and earnings per share growth of 13%. The company's USD67 billion investment plan for 2026-30 includes plans to add approximately 30GW of new capacity through 2035. Louisiana drives growth with approximately 60% demand increase expected by 2030. HSBC considers execution risk low, citing the company's early supply chain management and standardized processes.

2. Pinnacle West (PNW) - HSBC rates Pinnacle West as Buy with a target price of USD119.50, implying 15.5% upside. The Arizona-based integrated utility is forecasted to achieve 2026-30 rate base growth of 12% and earnings per share growth of 13%. The company has recorded growth rates of 5% to 10% in the last six quarters and forecasts approximately 45% demand increase by 2030. HSBC notes execution risk as medium to high due to past regulatory challenges, but expects material improvements following a pivotal ratemaking decision before year-end 2026.

3. NextEra (NEE) - HSBC rates NextEra as Buy with a target price of USD103.00, implying 29.1% upside. The company targets capital expenditures of USD295-325 billion over 2025-32, with USD185-225 billion allocated to NextEra Energy Resources.

CoreWeave Falls 4% as HSBC Reiterates Bearish Call on Debt Risk; Nebius Drops 5%, Oracle Holds Steady
sum: HSBC is doubling down on its bearish call against CoreWeave just as credit markets start flashing distress signals, and the selloff is spreading to a rival that was never even named in the note.

Debt-funded AI cloud providers are back under pressure as concerns about borrowing costs spread across the group. First of all, CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) shares are down 4% to $58.67 in morning trading.

Moreover, Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS | NBIS Price Prediction) shares are falling harder, down 5% to $162.20. However, Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) stock is only down 0.52% to $128.95, a comparatively steady contrast to the slide in CoreWeave and Nebius shares.

That split shows strain concentrated in the most debt-reliant corner of AI infrastructure, where CoreWeave and Nebius both operate. With its far broader revenue base, Oracle stock sits outside the worst of the selling.

HSBC repeated its Reduce rating on CoreWeave in a note on Monday. The accompanying price target sits well below where CoreWeave shares last closed, leaving little doubt about the direction of that call.

CoreWeave’s central challenge is revenue per megawatt of capacity, which could trail what larger cloud providers earn. Those bigger rivals offer broader services. They serve more diversified customers, giving them more ways to make money from each data center they run. Scale matters here, because bigger platforms can spread their costs across many products.
Two more pressure points weigh on CoreWeave. Slower growth at AI model developers could soften demand for short-term capacity, and rising borrowing costs make new infrastructure harder to finance.

Hong Kong Stocks Tumble After China's Golden Week Holiday; Hang Seng Tech Index Hits Two-Year Low as HSBC and Standard Chartered Lead Declines
sum: Hong Kong stocks faced pronounced profit-taking pressure on the first trading day after China's Golden Week holiday ended and A-shares and the Stock Connect resumed trading on October 8. The Hang Seng Tech Index plunged 2.89% on Thursday (October 8) to close at 4,073.38 points, its lowest level since September 2024. The Hang Seng Index fell 1.43% in tandem to close at 23,785.79 points, breaching the 24,000-point threshold. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index slipped 0.89%, narrowly holding above the 8,000-point round-number level.

Market participants noted that today's decline was driven by multiple converging forces. Selling pressure on Hong Kong-listed bank stocks intensified in the afternoon session, with heavyweight HSBC Holdings (0005.HK) tumbling nearly 5% to its lowest level since mid-June. Standard Chartered (2888.HK) fell even harder at 5.5%. The two bank stocks together dragged the Hang Seng Index down by more than 100 points, making them the primary source of the market's decline.

The sell-off in HSBC and Standard Chartered was not driven by a single negative catalyst. Surging global long-dated bond yields were the primary pressure point: UK 30-year government bond yields broke above 6% in early October, hitting their highest level since 1998, while US, German, and Japanese long-dated yields also hovered near multi-year highs, pushing up discount rates and compressing the valuation of bond holdings on bank balance sheets. The UK is scheduled to release its autumn budget on October 28, and the market expects the government may raise the bank surcharge. The Chancellor of the Exchequer has already convened meetings with executives from major banks but stopped short of pledging no tax increases. HSBC derives approximately 22% of its profits from the UK, while Standard Chartered's exposure is only about 3% to 5%, creating a notable divergence in sensitivity to tax changes. Additionally, the Financial Times reported that HSBC plans to cut nearly 70% of financial advisors in its UK wealth management division and replace them with AI-driven client services, raising concerns about client and asset attrition.

HSBC shares have been flying. So why are they falling now?
sum: HSBC (LSE: HSBA) shares have been flying this year. But after reaching a 52-week high in August, the stock has fallen around 10%.

Has the market simply decided the shares had got ahead of themselves, or is this just a temporary breather after a stunning run? With the wider banking sector also coming under pressure, there are plenty of reasons for investors to wonder what's going on.
For me though, the important question isn't whether HSBC shares can keep rising at the same pace. It's whether this recent pullback has changed the long-term investment case.
One thing that stands out to me is how much the bank has changed in recent years.
It's been busy shedding businesses and markets that don't fit its strategy and concentrating its resources on areas where it believes it can generate better returns.
Since 2025, it has announced 15 business or market exits, the most recent being the sale of the Singapore insurance business
At the same time, it's beefing up cost targets from its simplification programme. It's now expecting $2bn by the end of 2026.
